answer:
Evidence supports the claim through multiple sources:

- [NL-018-S04] reports that scanned, image-only PDFs still fail citation mapping after an update: citations point to page one of a 200-page document or page one of a 150-page document instead of the correct page, unlike natively digital PDFs.
- [NL-021-S02] ticket data shows 112 of 412 support tickets (27%) in May 2026 were ingestion/OCR issues; 40–50% of enterprise files are scanned PDFs without a text layer, causing TutorChat to return answers with no source citations or citations pointing to the entire document, e.g., page 1 of a 250-page PDF.
- [NL-011-S05] states that remaining citation tickets in May and June are "almost entirely linked to scanned, image-only PDFs" because TutorChat struggles to establish citation anchors and links to the start of the file rather than the specific page.
- [NL-006-S03] explains that scanned PDFs require OCR; without OCR, citations cannot be generated, and OCR is heuristic, so blurry or complex scans cause broken citations and retrieval gaps.
- [NL-006-S04] lists "low-resolution scanned PDF" as a root cause for "No citation available" or broken links because the layout parser cannot determine the exact page or section ID.
- [NL-021-S05] shows scanned PDFs flagged at low citation confidence, e.g., "45% Citation Confidence," with a warning that ingesting an image-only file without OCR "may result in poor citation quality."
- [NL-028-S03] states that low-quality scanned PDFs may prevent the system from generating page-specific citations due to OCR limitations.
